summary: The pilot preserves the deployed call sequence and explicit gates. Two failure-path issues require correction: bounded post-kill reaping and saving failing UART evidence before cleanup.
checks: Read pilot, tests, README, contract and validation.
Checked paired schema/order, cold/warm lifetimes, RX/TX hooks, target classification, bounds, gates and cleanup against source.
limitations: Read-only review; no hardware imports, devices, runtime tests, network or production operations.
15 passing tests and import-only evidence were not independently rerun.
Hardware cleanup, kernel behavior and reproduction fidelity remain unverified.

findings.evidence: stop_children kills and then calls unbounded proc.wait() for each child before proceeding to the next. An uninterruptible first child prevents signaling its peer and writing the final summary; parent ignores signals during final cleanup.
findings.requested_change: Signal every remaining child before waiting, bound post-kill reaping, record surviving/unreaped PIDs, finish failed summary, restore handlers even on cleanup errors. Add mocked unkillable-process coverage.

findings.evidence: UART capture is saved only after connectionShutdown/root.stop; cleanup hanging after a caught allocation exception loses the failing segment on forced termination.
findings.requested_change: Save best-effort non-draining raw snapshot immediately on failure before cleanup; keep final capture and record write errors. Test allocation GCP timeout plus hanging root.stop.
